chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If a tooth is struck, one waits with it for a year. If it falls out, the striker is made liable for five hundred dirhams; and if it does not fall out but turns black, he is made liable for two-thirds of its indemnity.

key_terms.أُغْرِمَ: was made financially liable or required to pay compensation
key_terms.اَلسِّنُّ: the tooth that has been injured
key_terms.خَمْسَمِائَةَ دِرْهَمٍ: five hundred dirhams as the specified compensation
key_terms.سَنَةً: a period of one year to wait before final judgment on the injury
key_terms.وَاسْوَدَّتْ: it turned black as a result of the injury

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah ruling if a tooth is struck and later falls out or turns black?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding injury to a tooth and the indemnity due for the resulting harm. It distinguishes between the tooth falling out after a waiting period and remaining in place while turning black, assigning different levels of compensation accordingly.
